request: There is no cheap way to see how many items exist without fetching the whole list. Add a GET /api/items/count route that returns the number of items as JSON. Add a test for it against the local database, and make sure the app still builds and the API still responds.

plan.goal: Give a client a lightweight endpoint that reports how many items the database holds.

scope.title: A GET /api/items/count route
scope.description: Add a GET /api/items/count handler to the Hono app in src/worker/index.ts that counts the rows in the items table and returns a JSON object with a count field. Register it before the catch-all asset route so the API path is matched, not served as an asset. Extend test/api.test.ts to cover an empty table and a table with items.

steps.description: Add app.get('/api/items/count', ...) to src/worker/index.ts above the catch-all asset route.
Count the rows with Drizzle and return c.json({ count }) with a 200 status.
Extend test/api.test.ts with a case that asserts the count is zero on an empty table and increases after a create, then run the build and both test suites.

out_of_scope.item: Showing the count on the items page
out_of_scope.reason: The request is an API endpoint that reports the count; surfacing it in the UI can follow as its own change.

out_of_scope.item: Counting with a filter or grouping
out_of_scope.reason: A single total is enough for a cheap count; filtered counts need query parameters that are not requested.
